This guide explains: This learning guide explains the completed project, its measured results, the reasons behind the student-selected decisions, and the concepts needed to discuss it without referring to the code. It is an explicitly AI-generated learning tool, separate from the student-authored interpretation in REPORT.md. Its explanatory prose was revised with Walter Writes and checked for accuracy by Codex.
First understand: Begin with the business arithmetic on pages 2 and 8. Next, review the feature definitions on page 4 and the shared model on pages 5-6. Finally, practice the demonstration and questions on pages 10-12. You need to express the tradeoffs in your own words, rather than memorize a script.
The student chose a bank: The student selected a bank calling team that must prioritize customers before a planned call. The target is whether a customer subscribed to a term deposit during the historical campaign. The model estimates a subscription probability, followed by a separate decision about whether to call.
For example, 20 calls: For example, 20 calls and 3 missed subscribers cost 20 × 2 + 3 × 50 = EUR 190. Accuracy is not the primary policy objective. Under these assumptions, a false negative is significantly more costly than an unnecessary call.
The supplied dictionary: The supplied dictionary indicates that rows are ordered chronologically from May 2008 through November 2010. Exact dates and customer IDs are missing. We maintain the original row order rather than invent dates or sort by month, which would mix different years.
<b>Training:</b>: During training, we learn imputations, numeric means and standard deviations, the one-hot vocabulary and model parameters. During validation, we compare a small set of feature and regularization choices and select the threshold. Testing evaluates those frozen choices. Adjusting the test threshold to improve the reported result would invalidate that final comparison.
If pdays=999: If pdays=999 and previous=0, the recency indicator, log recency and log previous contacts are all zero. The sentinel is replaced before the recency log transformation, while log(1 + 0)=0 handles the contact count. If pdays=3 and previous=2, the values are 1, log(4)=1.386 and log(3)=1.099. These values are shown before numeric standardization.
All three implementations are <b>: Each implementation uses logistic regression. None includes hidden layers, trees or neural-network feature extractors. PyTorch is a machine-learning framework; using it does not automatically turn a model into deep learning.
The weighted sum z: The weighted sum z can take any real value. The sigmoid maps it to a probability between 0 and 1. The intercept b is the score when numeric inputs are at their training means and the other encoded inputs are zero. With full one-hot encoding, this is not a literal typical customer.
The first term is binary: The first term is binary cross-entropy, also called log loss. It penalizes confidently wrong probabilities strongly. The second term, L2 regularization, encourages smaller weights and helps stabilize fitting with redundant or correlated encoded features. The intercept is not regularized. No class weights are assigned; changing them would alter the objective and complicate probability interpretation.
A gradient tells: A gradient tells us how sensitive the objective is to each parameter. Gradient descent subtracts learning_rate × gradient from each parameter. Autograd computes these derivatives from the computation graph. The tests independently compare its gradients with analytical expressions and finite-difference approximations.
Scaling changes: Scaling changes numeric units for optimization and regularization. Feature engineering changes the relationships a model can express. A linear score on transformed inputs can capture log-count effects and category interactions while remaining logistic regression in its parameters.
Using the same numeric C: Identical numerical values for C and lambda would not produce equivalent objectives. The equivalence test checks that the shared PyTorch objective has a gradient close to zero at scikit-learn's solution.
In more detail, augment: Add a column of ones to X for the intercept. For logistic loss, curvature is bounded by 0.25 times the largest eigenvalue of X_aug.T @ X_aug / n. Adding lambda gives a conservative upper bound on curvature for the penalized objective.
The project uses the original UCI: I chose UCI's Bank Marketing dataset, specifically bank-additional-full.csv. It contains 41,188 client/campaign entries, 20 original inputs and a single binary target, y (term-deposit subscription). According to the supplied data dictionary, the entries are ordered by date from May 2008 through November 2010. Each entry contains customer characteristics and campaign-contact summaries, but exact timestamps and customer identifiers are not provided.
The project assumes the customer profile: The implementation includes age; job, marital status, education, default, housing and loan categories; and prior-campaign outcome. It excludes duration, completed-campaign contact count, and final-call channel/month/weekday because the file does not establish their availability before the planned call. I also excluded macroeconomic series because publication-time and vintage information are absent. Although this limits the available predictive signal, it makes the information boundary explicit. Customer profiles and prior-campaign history are assumed to exist in the CRM before a new call.
There are no blank cells: Numeric inputs are median-imputed defensively and standardized using training statistics. One-hot encoding uses the training vocabulary and retains unknown; unseen categories are handled without refitting. There are no blank fields, but some categories are unknown, including 8,597 default and 1,731 education values. The 12 exact duplicate rows are retained because, without identifiers, identical attributes cannot reliably distinguish accidental duplication from distinct customers. No rows were deleted. The 4,110 sentinel/history inconsistencies are documented and preserved. The recency_recorded indicator identifies a recorded day interval; previous and poutcome retain the other history information.
The raw data remains unchanged: To evaluate later campaigns, I selected the entire ordered version of the file. At 5,834,924 bytes, it is practical to commit and retrain, although its 41,188 rows exceed the assignment's approximate 20k-row guideline. I left the CSV unaltered, with provenance described in data/README.md and its SHA-256 hash in artifacts/metadata.json. There is no runtime data download.
The student selected history_context: I evaluated three feature recipes and three regularization strengths. The raw representation serves as a control that treats 999 as an ordinary number. After reviewing the validation results, I chose the engineered representation with the appropriate sentinel meaning, even though the raw control produced slightly lower validation log loss. The best engineered configuration is selected using validation log loss. I am not claiming that the engineered features improve the measured score over the raw control.
The baseline always predicts: The naive probability baseline predicts the training prevalence, 0.048074, for each record. At the frozen threshold, it calls everyone. The explicit decision baselines cost EUR 16,476 for call-all and EUR 127,000 for call-none on test. Call-all and call-none are decision policies, not useful probability forecasts. Their full metric rows are included in the export, but their clipped hard-probability log losses should not be used to evaluate probability quality.
Codex wrote and debugged: Codex implemented and debugged the code, tests and dashboard, formatted evidence, and authored this AI-generated guide. The student selected the topic, decision point, cost assumptions, split strategy, feature ideas and semantic tradeoff, and supplied the recommendation. Walter Writes revised prose, with factual corrections by Codex. The student remains responsible for understanding the work.
There were three feature recipes: This is a small, inspectable comparison of three feature recipes and three L2 strengths (0.001, 0.01 and 0.1), evaluated on the same validation block. The held-out test was not used to make these choices.
If probabilities were perfectly: With perfectly calibrated probabilities and correct simplified cost assumptions, calling costs EUR 2 while skipping costs 50 × p in expectation. Calling is therefore preferred when p exceeds 2/50=0.04. The empirical validation threshold differs slightly because validation observations are finite and probability calibration is imperfect.
A follow-up could assess: A follow-up could assess successive later campaign periods, check calibration with a recent validation block, verify the real cost and value assumptions, and obtain customer IDs and exact timestamps. These changes require a later untouched evaluation period. Keep the original test results documented rather than replacing them with tuned results.
Training saves the preprocessing: Training stores the preprocessor, scikit-learn model, raw PyTorch tensors, standard PyTorch state_dict and naive baseline. It also exports predictions, metrics, coefficients, split membership, experiment results and training traces. The dashboard reads those files; app.py never calls a fitting routine.
The checks verify:: The checks cover forbidden-field isolation, sentinel and unknown handling, chronological partitioning and training-only statistics, analytical and finite-difference gradient agreement, objective equivalence, persisted predictions and agreement across methods, threshold endpoints and ties, validation-only threshold selection, inference with fitting disabled, and reproduction of exported dashboard costs.
Be able to reconstruct: Reconstruct the EUR 1,406 comparison, explain why the cost-based threshold is low, derive C=1/(n*lambda), and identify which information was excluded from the pre-call decision. Practice the five-step dashboard demonstration. Check that the report conclusion reflects what you personally think.
Economic indicators are excluded: Economic indicators were excluded conservatively. The dataset provides observed values but no publication-time or revision-vintage information. Excluding them sacrifices potentially useful signal. This is an availability decision, not a claim that macroeconomic conditions are irrelevant.
This is response prediction: This is response prediction, not causal uplift modeling. Everyone in the historical campaign was exposed to marketing in some form. We cannot observe what would have happened without calling, so we cannot claim the policy creates deposits or measures actual profit.
The intended use is later: The intended use is future campaigns. Randomly mixing early and late records could expose training to future conditions, making chronology more relevant even when results are less flattering. Because exact timestamps are absent, a split boundary may cut through a day or campaign. Separation of repeated customers cannot be guaranteed either.
Data-quality caveat:: A data-quality caveat: 4,110 records have pdays=999 despite previous>0. The indicator therefore means recency recorded, not never contacted. The count and prior outcome are preserved rather than silently rewriting history.
Numeric values are median: Numeric fields are median-imputed defensively and standardized using training statistics: z=(x-training mean)/training standard deviation. No numeric values are missing, so imputation does not alter this dataset. Unknown categories are retained, rather than replaced by a frequent known category. The fitted encoder safely ignores unseen categories, but that does not mean the model understands them.
The selected recipe has: The selected recipe uses 46 encoded columns. The implementation whitelists allowed inputs, preventing the target and excluded fields from entering the feature matrix. Automated tests perturb forbidden fields and verify that the features remain unchanged.
<b>ROC-AUC:</b>: ROC-AUC measures how often a subscriber ranks above a non-subscriber. Average precision summarizes the precision-recall relationship; the constant baseline score here equals the test subscriber rate, 0.308327. Log loss measures probability error with strong penalties for confident mistakes. Brier measures mean squared probability error.
These are the weights stated: These grading weights are those listed in the repository when inspected; the brief describes them as a proposal subject to confirmation. Both main.py commands must run without manual intervention. REPORT.md supplies evidence for the weighted components rather than receiving a separate grade component.
<b>Answers:</b>: Answers: A: EUR 400. B: C halves. C: Yes. Both frameworks may share poor features, a distribution mismatch, invalid business assumptions or an unsuitable decision rule. Agreement alone does not establish business value.
